pos.personaBrief: Aragones and Del Bosque built on toque de balon ('el que es dueño del balón es dueño del juego'), with Spain dominating possession at Euro 2012 and conceding one goal; possession was also protection.

pro.personaBrief: Spain passed patiently in small areas with a safe double pivot (Busquets, Alonso) and varied sideways passing, though Torres was fed straight balls in behind in the 2012 final and the 2008 counters were incisive.

est.personaBrief: Fabregas as a false nine, Silva and Iniesta moving inside and Xavi's tight passing show fluid, relational play concentrated in small areas, though a defined double pivot anchored the shape.

lar.personaBrief: Spain packed the middle with Xavi, Iniesta, Silva, Alonso and Busquets, used a six-man midfield in 2012 and cut inside rather than hugging the line; Navas and wide play were secondary and full-backs gave some width.

blo.personaBrief: Villa was the first defender, Torres pressed Irish defenders high, and Spain kept the ball so rivals exhausted themselves, with a high line and quick regain after losses.

mar.personaBrief: Marking evidence is thin; Spain defended by keeping the ball and collective pressing in space, with no dedicated star-markers, and corners were mixed.

pla.personaBrief: Del Bosque kept the possession game ('es nuestro estilo, que nos ha dado todo') whoever the opponent was, only tweaking the shape (double pivot, false nine) rather than studying rivals first.

res.personaBrief: Spain won trophies with a controlled, attractive style and attacked for the win away; 'how' mattered to Aragones and Del Bosque, who defended their style, though results were also central.

sis.personaBrief: A collective of great players ('grandes individualidades al servicio del grupo'); Villa as first defender, same starting XI, defined roles for all but built on high talent.

jog.personaBrief: Small technical midfielders (Xavi, Iniesta, Silva) at the heart; Spain lacked height and relied on passing, and the pivot was valued for passing over brawn.

bas.personaBrief: A veteran core of ever-present players (Casillas, Xavi, Ramos, Alonso) kept their places; Del Bosque left the door open to Raul and favored proven players while using some youth.

lid.personaBrief: Del Bosque stressed good relations with everyone, handled Barca-Madrid tension, kept a united group (Casillas hosting card nights), listened to leaders and cared for people over orders.
